headline: A Waterloo, Ontario, auto repair shop has put a humanoid robot named Cory at its front counter.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 1: only a short video description was readable, so what the robot does is unverified.
importance_line: It points to humanoid robots reaching small customer-facing businesses, but CBC does not say what the robot does or how well it works.
summary: CBC reports that Columbia Auto Group, a car repair shop in Waterloo, Ontario, now greets customers at its counter with a humanoid robot called Cory, built with Cory AI, a Canadian-owned AI developer. CBC Kitchener-Waterloo reporter Lauren Kuivenhoven visited the shop to see the robot at work, but CBC's short description does not say which tasks it handles.
